title: What made the first transcontinental railroad so important?
sources: National Museum of American History Transcontinental Railroad

lines.text: Before eighteen sixty-nine, traveling from New York to California meant six grueling months in a covered wagon.
Thousands died from cholera, starvation, and freezing blizzards crossing the wilderness.
Then, thousands of Chinese and Irish laborers blasted railroad tunnels through solid granite Sierra Nevada mountains with nitroglycerin.
lines.caps: Laborers blasted *tunnels | through solid granite with *nitroglycerin

lines.text: They laid nearly two thousand miles of iron track by hand, meeting at Promontory Summit, Utah, with the famous Golden Spike.
lines.caps: Connected the *nation | with the famous *Golden Spike!

lines.text: Instantly, a six-month deadly trek was transformed into a comfortable seven-day train ride for just sixty-five dollars.
It united the American continent, created standard time zones, and launched America into an industrial superpower.
lines.caps: Created standard *time zones | and forged a *superpower!

lines.text: Those two ribbons of steel created the modern United States.
lines.caps: Ribbons of *steel | that unified an entire *nation!
